description: A character and political-history essay on Teal'c: the First Prime's defection, Bra'tac's hidden rebellion, the price paid by his family, Jaffa biological dependency, and the transition from overthrowing false gods to building self-government.

related_resources.reason: Jaffa High Council representation, referendum, Ba'al mind-control and elections.
Character first appears as Apophis's First Prime and changes sides in the Chulak prison.
Bra'tac, rite of M'al Sharran, Teal'c memories, Va'lar and the prison defection.
First-season Teal'c family, Rya'c and dependence on larval symbiote.
Rya'c brainwashing, Drey'auc and Fro'tak, family risk.
Drey'auc dies refusing a replacement symbiote, Rya'c confronts Teal'c.
Christopher Judge writing credit, Ishta, Moloc, Rya'c and Kar'yn marriage.
Kytano and Imhotep; Christopher Judge story credit and Peter DeLuise teleplay credit.
Christopher Judge writing credit, Teal'c dream, symbiote and tretonin transition.
Firsthand Teal'c development and writing recollection.
Injury and recovery on tretonin, Rya'c and Bra'tac rescue.
Debate on taking Dakara and the Jaffa rebellion coalition.
Free Jaffa Nation formation, Dakara, Bra'tac and Teal'c political choice.
Gerak, Ori conversion, the Jaffa crisis and intervention to save people on Earth.

historical_claims.anchor: Late in *Stargate SG-1*, Teal'c sits at a council table on the planet Dakara, trying to persuade other Jaffa leaders that their government should be chosen by the people.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: On Chulak in the television pilot, *Children of the Gods*, the members of SG-1 find themselves among prisoners selected for the pleasure of the Goa'uld Apophis.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: *Threshold*, from the fifth season, returns to the years before Teal'c's defection and corrects any temptation to treat the decision as spontaneous.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: Ordered to execute a fellow Jaffa named Va'lar, Teal'c lets him escape and deceives Apophis with evidence that the order was carried out.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: In *Bloodlines*, Teal'c tries to prevent Rya'c from undergoing the Jaffa ceremony in which a larval symbiote is implanted.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: *Family*, in the second season, makes that hardship still sharper.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: In the sixth-season opening, *Redemption*, we learn that Drey'auc has died after refusing to accept another larval symbiote when hers matured.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: By *Sacrifices*, he has another parental problem: Rya'c intends to marry Kar'yn, a young Jaffa warrior, and Teal'c thinks the marriage premature.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: In *The Warrior*, a charismatic commander named Kytano draws followers with the promise of uniting the Jaffa against the Goa'uld.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: He turns out to be the Goa'uld Imhotep himself, using the rebellion as another means of gathering power.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: In *Birthright* and *Sacrifices*, Ishta and the Hak'tyl fight against Moloc, whose rule has put female Jaffa children in mortal danger.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: The symbiote problem comes to the foreground in *The Changeling*, an episode written by Christopher Judge.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: In *Orpheus*, after Teal'c is injured, his recovery is slow and his confidence suffers.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: In *Reckoning*, with the Goa'uld in crisis and the Replicators threatening everyone, Teal'c and Bra'tac urge their fellow rebels to seize it.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: Dakara becomes the symbolic center of a new Free Jaffa Nation.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: Gerak ultimately chooses to save people at enormous cost to himself, but his defection from one belief to another exposes how fragile the new order remains.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note

historical_claims.anchor: Then comes *Stronghold*. Teal'c and Bra'tac argue for a referendum to replace a High Council whose seats are linked to military might.
historical_claims.source_locator: Episode guide, credited interview or associated production note
